### Bellvitge coordinates in Spain a trail of a self-administered injection that improves myasthenia gravis from the first week onward

  * Improvements in daily activities were observed from the first week, while improvements in muscle strength were seen from the fourth week.
  * The international trial, published in JAMA Neurology, included 260 patients from 113 centres across 20 countries.
  * Bellvitge cares for around 450 people with myasthenia gravis and currently has three active studies on this rare diseases.

Image: Miastenia Bellvitge_NOTI

GO BACK

  * Speaking, chewing, swallowing, walking, or keeping one’s arms raised can become difficult tasks for people living with myasthenia gravis. Muscle weakness typically worsens with repeated movement and often becomes more noticeable as the day progresses. The Bellvitge Universitary Hospital and IDIBELL coordinated Spain’s participation in PREVAIL, an international phase 3 clinical trial evaluating gefurulimab, an experimental treatment for adults with generalized myasthenia gravis who have antibodies against the acetylcholine receptor, the most common form of the disease.The trial enrolled 260 patients from 113 centers in 20 countries. International collaboration is particularly important in rare diseases, as it allows researchers to recruit enough participants to generate robust results. Findings published in JAMA Neurology showed that patients receiving the experimental treatment experienced greater improvements than those receiving placebo. Improvements in daily activities began to be observed during the first week, while clinical improvements in muscle strength became evident from the fourth week onward. These benefits were maintained throughout the six-month study period.Dr. Carles Casasnovas, neurologist at the Neuromuscular Diseases Unit of Hospital de Bellvitge and researcher at the Neurometabolic diseases group at IDIBELL and CIBERER, served as the study coordinator in Spain and principal investigator at Bellvitge. Dr. Velina Nedkova and Dr. Moisés Morales also participated as sub-investigators. 

Improvements in muscle strength and daily function

After six months, 46.3% of patients receiving the experimental treatment achieved the muscle-strength improvement threshold defined as a response criterion in the study, compared with 25.2% in the placebo group. In other words, nearly half of treated patients responded, compared with one quarter of those who received placebo.

For daily activities, nearly two-thirds of treated patients (65.5%) achieved the predefined improvement criterion, compared with 52.2% of patients in the placebo group.

“These improvements are important because they can translate into fewer symptoms and greater ability to carry out everyday activities,” explains Dr. Casasnovas.

The incidence of adverse events was similar in both groups. Bellvitge continues to participate in the extension phase of the trial, which will provide additional data on the long-term effects and safety of the treatment.

The treatment is administered as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection that patients or caregivers can give at home. If approved and incorporated into clinical practice, this approach could provide greater autonomy, eliminate the need for regular travel to healthcare facilities, and reduce dependence on hospital day-care units for treatment administration.

 

A rare disease affecting nearly 450 Bellvitge patients

Myasthenia gravis is a chronic autoimmune disease that disrupts communication between nerves and muscles. It causes muscle weakness and fatigue, which worsen with activity and improve with rest. The condition can occur at any age but is more common in women under 40 and men over 60 years of age. It may also cause drooping eyelids, double vision and, in the most severe cases, respiratory difficulties.

According to the Spanish Society of Neurology, more than 16,000 people live with myasthenia gravis in Spain. Although there is currently no cure, available treatments can control symptoms and allow many patients to lead a normal or near-normal life. Research remains essential to expand therapeutic options and better tailor them to individual patient needs.

The Neuromuscular Diseases Unit at Bellvitge cares for approximately 450 people with myasthenia gravis. The unit has participated in four clinical trials on the disease and currently has three ongoing studies. The hospital is a national reference center (CSUR) for rare neuromuscular diseases and is part of both the Catalan and European reference networks.

This research is part of REMMA Bellvitge, IDIBELL’s research program specifically dedicated to rare adult diseases. The program bridges research and clinical care to improve diagnosis and accelerate patient access to new treatments. Participation in international studies such as PREVAIL is one of the keyways to speed up the arrival of new therapeutic alternatives for patients.

The PREVAIL trial was funded by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease, which participated in the study design and development, data analysis, and manuscript preparation.

 

 

 

About Bellvitge University Hospital

Bellvitge University Hospital is a public, university-affiliated, research-driven and innovative hospital. With more than 5,200 highly qualified and committed professionals, it serves as the local hospital for residents of L’Hospitalet de Llobregat and El Prat de Llobregat, while also acting as a highly specialized referral center for two million people across southern Catalonia. It performs more complex surgical procedures than any other hospital in Catalonia, particularly in oncological surgery, and is a member of the Bellvitge Health Campus, recognized by the Organisation of European Cancer Institutes (OECI) as a Comprehensive Cancer Centre for excellence in cancer care, research and education. The hospital integrates patient experience into all its projects and promotes close collaboration with primary care and neighboring hospitals. Focused on personalized medicine, it offers state-of-the-art genetic and imaging diagnostic technologies for cancer and rare diseases, complemented by its High Precision Diagnostic Center, home to the first PET/MRI system in Spain’s public healthcare network. Each year, the hospital performs approximately 26,000 major surgeries, records 39,000 admissions, delivers 400,000 outpatient visits and conducts around 100,000 diagnostic tests.

 

About IDIBELL

The Bellvitge Biomedical Research Institute (IDIBELL) is a research center established in 2004 and specialized in cancer, neuroscience, translational medicine and regenerative medicine. It brings together more than 1,500 professionals working across 73 research groups and publishes over 1,400 scientific articles annually. IDIBELL is jointly governed by Bellvitge University Hospital, Viladecans Hospital of the Catalan Health Institute, the Catalan Institute of Oncology, the University of Barcelona, and the City Council of L’Hospitalet de Llobregat. The institute is a member of the University of Barcelona International Excellence Campus (HUBc) and part of the CERCA network of research centers supported by the Government of Catalonia. In 2009, it became one of the first five Spanish research centers accredited as a Health Research Institute by the Carlos III Health Institute. IDIBELL also participates in the European Union’s HR Excellence in Research program and is a member of EATRIS and REGIC. Since 2018, it has been an Accredited Centre of the AECC Scientific Foundation (FCAECC).

Title: PET Quantification-Preserving Registration for Longitudinal Whole-Body PSMA PET/CT
Authors: Fryderyk Kögl, Anna Reithmeir, Daniel M. Lang, Emily Chan, Rickmer Braren, Julia A. Schnabel
Date: Thu Oct 15 07:54:21 2026

We adapt the diffeomorphic coarse-to-fine LapIRN architecture for longitudinal whole-body PSMA PET/CT registration in the Learn2Reg 2026 PSMAReg challenge. The method combines affine pre-registration, multi-modal deformable registration, and test-time instance optimization. We further introduce PET biomarker preservation losses for metabolic tumor volume (MTV) and total lesion glycolysis (TLG), including Jacobian-based constraints, and a per-structure rigidity regularization for skeletal structures. The submitted configuration achieved 81.0% DSC and 6.17 mm HD95, with MTV and TLG errors of 3.3% and 3.3%, respectively, on our evaluation protocol. Code is available at https://github.com/koegl/psmareg.

# Intraoperative detection of oral squamous cell carcinoma margins in dogs using cathepsin-activated near-infrared (NIR) imaging

October 21, 2026

Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is a common cancer of the epidermis, or outer layer of the skin, and oral tissues in dogs. The skin, oral cavity, and digits are the most common sites of SCC. In this study, we will be assessing dogs with oral SCC. Surgical excision of the tumor is regarded as the best treatment option for local disease control.

The aim of this study is to improve detection of surgical margins at the time of surgery to remove the tumor. This is vital in both veterinary and human surgical oncology to minimize the chance of local recurrence. We are using a new near-infrared (NIR) imaging agent, injected intravenously, and a novel imaging system to identify the tumor and its margins during surgery. This imaging adds no more than 15 minutes to a surgical procedure.

Eligibility:

  * Dogs with diagnosed oral SCC that are eligible for surgical excision
  * No prior/current treatments (including surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy) for this cancer
  * No other significant health concerns that are an immediate threat to life outside of trial.
  * Ability to attend visits at PennVet in Philadelphia

Benefits:

$3000 paid towards the cost of surgery.

Contact the VCIC at 215-573-0302 or email vcic@vet.upenn.edu for more information.

Title: AI Consilium: a Benchmark of LLM Clinical Multidisciplinary Second Opinions
Authors: Alexey A. Bokov, Ivan I. Panin, Nikolay B. Nechaev, Mikhail Yu. Valkov, Valeria Yu. Chernina, Natalia Gombolevskaya, Ayyaz Hussain, Vladimir M. Agafonov, Victor A. Gombolevskiy, Aleksandr V. Nesterov, Iaroslav R. Bespalov, Ivan V. Oseledets, Dmitry V. Dylov
Date: Thu Oct 15 17:46:37 2026

Large language models (LLMs) can generate differential diagnoses for complex cases, but a useful second opinion must also be factually grounded, clinically coherent, actionable, and safe. We developed a multidimensional benchmark using 300 diagnostically resolved NEJM--MedQA cases: 110 for physician reference ratings and Judge calibration and 190 for held-out evaluation. Eight single-model pipelines generated independent role-specific opinions and interactive-consilium reports under free-form and structured clinical-reasoning conditions. A physician-calibrated LLM Judge evaluated 3,040 final reports and the corresponding structured primary-role outputs. Model identity separated report quality more strongly than response format. Structured final reports had higher overall mean scores in seven of eight model pipelines, with their clearest advantage in management (2.740 vs. 2.436). Compared with the structured pre-consilium primary-role opinion, the complete structured synthesis had higher pooled scores across all five shared criteria, with the largest increases in problem prioritization, factual grounding, and reasoning coherence. GPT-5.6-Sol led every evaluated component and reached consensus in the fewest review rounds. These findings show that the benchmark can distinguish model capability, the contribution of multidisciplinary synthesis, criterion-specific effects of response structure, deliberation dynamics, and inference requirements within one common-case evaluation.

leads.title: From Adults to Children: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Chest X-Ray Classification under Domain Shift

search_hits.retrieved_snippet:
【turn1055academia57】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 6 days ago; 
Title: From Adults to Children: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Chest X-Ray Classification under Domain Shift
Authors: Sara Inácio, Hugo Proença, João C. Neves
Date: Thu Oct 15 12:57:08 2026

Foundation models have shown significant potential across diverse fields and have been applied to medical imaging, but their robustness across patient populations remains unclear. In this work, we investigate foundation models' ability to generalize from adult to pediatric chest X-ray classification. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first benchmark to compare multiple foundation models under a common adult-to-pediatric evaluation setting while also analyzing the effect of adaptation depth. We harmonize VinDr-CXR and PediCXR into a five-label classification task and evaluate six foundation models and two CNN baselines. All models are adapted using adult data only and tested in both the in-domain and pediatric domains using linear probing, partial fine-tuning, and full fine-tuning. The benchmark reveals a clear and consistent trend: all models suffer a substantial performance degradation when transferred from adult to pediatric data, with drops exceeding 10 percentage points. While Macro-AUROC values reach approximately 92% on the adult test set, performance decreases to around 78% on the pediatric domain. Another important finding is that increasing the depth of adaptation does not significantly improve cross-population generalization. Moreover, strong in-domain performance does not translate into better performance on pediatric data.

### What is a cavernous malformation?

Cavernous malformations are made up of abnormal blood vessels. They are made of capillaries (the smallest blood vessels in the body). Blood moves through cavernous malformations very slowly. They look like raspberries and have very thin walls. Those thin walls can leak, and blood may enter nearby brain or spinal cord tissue. They are not cancerous but are sometimes called vascular tumors because they can grow.

#### Where they form

Most cavernous malformations occur in the cerebral lobes, the upper part of the brain. Cavernous malformations may also occur in the brainstem, the part of the brain that connects to the spinal cord. The spinal cord is the least common place for a cavernous malformation that causes symptoms. Cavernous malformations can cause severe symptoms and complications when they hemorrhage (bleed).

Image: A cavernous malformation removed during surgery. It looks like a small, dark red raspberry.

### What symptoms can a cavernous malformation cause?

Symptoms from cavernous malformations vary from person to person. Location plays a large role, since different parts of the brain and spinal cord control different functions. Size and behavior matter too — a small, stable cavernous malformation is less likely to cause symptoms than a larger one or one that is actively bleeding. Some cavernous malformations cause no symptoms at all.

If more than one cavernous malformation is found incidentally, it is a good idea to have regular follow-up visits with a doctor. This helps you maintain a relationship with a care provider in case you develop symptoms later.

Even though this can feel scary, it’s important to know that many stable lesions stay stable for years and never cause problems. Surgery is rarely used unless a lesion is causing symptoms, since surgery carries its own risks.

### What is a sporadic cavernous malformation?

Most cavernous malformations happen by chance and are not passed down in families. These are called sporadic cavernous malformations.

People with this type usually have:

  * Only one cavernous malformation
  * No family history of the condition

Family members, including children, of a person with sporadic cavernous malformation are not more likely to have cavernous malformations than anyone else.

#### How doctors check

To check for this condition, your doctor may order an MRI scan with a special type of image called susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI). This type of imaging can help doctors see smaller cavernous malformations. If no additional cavernous malformations are found on SWI, this is reassuring that the person likely has a sporadic cavernous malformation.

### What causes multiple cavernous malformations?

Some people have more than one cavernous malformation. This can happen for a few reasons:

  * The most common reason is familial cavernous malformation. People with this condition are born with a higher chance of developing multiple cavernous malformations over time. Familial cavernous malformation is caused by a mutation (change) in the CCM1 (also called KRIT1), CCM2, or CCM3 (also called PDCD10) genes.
  * Some people develop multiple cavernous malformations after radiation therapy for brain cancer.
Vanessa was two weeks into her second semester at fashion school in New York City when a brain bleed changed her life. An MRI traced the bleed to a cerebral cavernous malformation in her thalamus (a part of the brain that helps control movement and sensation), with two more nearby. All three lesions were clustered together around a developmental venous anomaly (DVA), which is not uncommon with cavernous malformations. Doctors often talk about bleeding risk in terms of yearly risk or five-year risk. Many cavernous malformations never cause a serious bleed. However, if a cavernous malformation has already bled once, the chance of another bleed is higher. The risk is greatest in the first five years after the first bleed, and then it slowly goes down over time and may return close to the level of cavernous malformations that have never bled. Very small cavernous malformations do not usually bleed.

Image: MRI showing a cavernous malformation in the brainstem

### Does anything increase my hemorrhage risk?

A bleed that causes new symptoms, also called a symptomatic hemorrhage, is the most serious problem that can happen with a cavernous malformation. About 1 in 4 people diagnosed with this condition will have at least one bleed.

#### Medicines and hormones

You may wonder if certain medications, like blood thinners, increase your risk. Current research shows that blood thinners do not seem to increase the risk of bleeding for most people. However, you should always talk with your healthcare provider before starting or stopping any medication.

For the most up-to-date information, visit the hemorrhage section of the Alliance to Cure Cavernous Malformation website. If you have questions about your own risk, talk with your healthcare provider. They can help you understand what is best for your situation.

Image: John

### Patient Story: John

Living with a Spinal Cavernous Malformation

John had already lived with a cavernous malformation diagnosis for four years when he boarded a flight home from a family trip. His brainstem CCM had bled once, leaving him with symptoms that improved over months but never fully resolved. He had learned to live with them.

[서울=뉴시스]이소헌 기자 = 보령이 회사가 개발 중인 항암신약의 임상 2상 환자 모집을 완료했다.
보령은 세계 최초로 혈액암 유발 물질인 PI3K 감마·델타·DNA-PK의 3중 저해 기전을 갖춘 항암신약 후보물질 '보스몰리십'(BR101801)의 임상 2상 환자 모집을 최근 완료했다고 19일 밝혔다.
보스몰리십은 암세포의 성장·생존 신호 및 DNA 손상 복구에 관여하는 PI3K 감마, PI3K 델타와 DNA-PK를 동시에 저해하는 퍼스트 인 클래스(First-In-Class) 항암신약물질이다.
성분명인 보스몰리십은 세계보건기구(WHO) 국제일반명(INN)에 등재된 명칭으로, 보령의 앞 글자 'Bo'와 우수한 저분자 화합물, PI3K 저해제 계열에 사용되는 접미사 'lisib'를 결합해 지었다고 회사는 설명했다.
이번 임상 2상은 재발성 또는 불응성 PTCL 환자를 대상으로 보스몰리십 단독요법의 항종양 효과, 안전성, 내약성을 평가하기 위한 단일군·다기관·공개 임상시험이다.
보령은 지난해 5월 식품의약품안전처로부터 2상 임상시험계획(IND)을 승인받았으며, 지난 3월 첫 환자 투약을 시작으로 국내 17개 임상시험 실시기관에서 총 44명의 환자를 대상으로 임상을 진행 중이다.
보령은 첫 환자 투약 이후 약 7개월 동안 목표 환자 44명 모집을 마쳤다. 보령은 향후 1년간의 추적 관찰을 거쳐 오는 2028년 임상 2상을 완료하고 품목허가를 신청할 계획이다.
보령에 따르면 보스몰리십은 미국 식품의약국(FDA)으로부터 PTCL의 하위 질환인 PTCL-NOS와 혈관면역모세포성 T세포 림프종에 대해 희귀의약품 지정을 받았으며, 국내 식품의약품안전처에서도 개발단계 희귀의약품으로 지정됐다.
국내 희귀의약품은 조건부 허가제도를 통해 임상 2상 완료 후 품목허가를 신청할 수 있어, 상용화 시점을 앞당겨 환자들의 치료 접근성을 높이고 새로운 치료 선택지를 보다 신속하게 제공할 수 있을 것으로 전망된다고 회사는 전했다.
김정균 보령 대표는 "말초 T세포 림프종 환자가 선택할 수 있는 치료 옵션이 될 수 있도록 1상에서 확인한 가능성을 2상 결과로 이어가는 한편, 빠르게 환자에게 제공할 수 있도록 향후 임상에 역량을 집중할 것"이라고 말했다.

测试候选治疗产品的临床试验通常分为四个阶段，整个开发过程所经历所有阶段通常会耗费数年时间。若药物顺利通过临床试验I、II和III期后，当局监管机构会批准候选产品用于普通患者。临床试验IV期是药物上市后继续研究或药物的持续监测研究，旨在监控药品上市后数年的安全性。

##### 台灣動物實驗管理面缺失

根據現行台灣《動物保護法》第 15 條：使用動物進行科學應用，應儘量避免使用活體動物，有使用之必要時，應以最少數目為之。但實際動物實驗管理層面卻不一定符合法規。

1、兔化豬瘟疫苗

台灣是豬瘟疫區，18 年來已犧牲超過 50 萬隻兔子製作「乾燥兔化豬瘟疫苗」。研究報告指出：目前已有不必犧牲活體動物生產的「組織培養」與「E2次單位」疫苗上市，但至今農委會卻不肯停止生產兔化豬瘟疫苗。不僅未落實3R 原則，更已違反《動物保護法》第 15 條「使用動物進行科學應用，應儘量避免使用活體動物，有使用之必要時，應以最少數目為之」的規定。

## 治疗

Title: ESG-Kor: A Korean Dataset for ESG-related Information Extraction and Practical Use Cases
Authors: Jaeyoung Lee, Geonyeong Son, Misuk Kim
Date: Thu Oct 15 06:48:21 2026

With the expansion of pre-trained language model usage in recent years, the importance of datasets for performing tasks in specialized domains has significantly increased. Therefore, we have built a Korean dataset called ESG-Kor to automatically extract Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) information, which has recently gained importance. ESG-Kor is a dataset consisting of a total of 118,946 sentences that extracted information on each ESG component from Korean companies' sustainability reports and manually labeled it according to objective rules provided by ESG evaluation agencies. To verify the effectiveness and applicability of the ESG-Kor dataset, classification performance was confirmed using several Korean pre-trained language models, and significant performance was obtained. Additionally, by extending the ESG classification model to documents of small and medium enterprises and extracting information based on ESG key issues and in-depth analysis, we demonstrated potential and practical use cases in the ESG field.

## Latest Animal Diseases MCQ Objective Questions

#### Animal Diseases Question 1:

विडाल परीक्षण पुष्टि करता है:

  1. मलेरिया
  2. टाइफाइड बुखार
  3. ​एड्स (AIDS)
  4. डेंगू

#### Answer (Detailed Solution Below)

Option 2 : टाइफाइड बुखार

#### Animal Diseases Question 1 Detailed Solution

सही उत्तर टाइफाइड बुखार है।

Imageमुख्य बिंदु

  * विडल टेस्ट एक सीरोलॉजिकल टेस्ट है जो टाइफाइड बुखार के निदान में मदद करता है, जो साल्मोनेला टाइफी या साल्मोनेला पैराटाइफी नामक जीवाणु के कारण होता है।
  * यह टेस्ट एस. टाइफी और एस. पैराटाइफी के एंटीजन के खिलाफ रोगी के रक्त में विशिष्ट एंटीबॉडी (एग्लूटीनिन) की उपस्थिति का पता लगाता है।
  * टाइफाइड बुखार दूषित भोजन और पानी के माध्यम से फैलता है और खराब स्वच्छता वाले क्षेत्रों में आम है।
  * विडल टेस्ट में एग्लूटिनेशन प्रतिक्रियाओं की जांच के लिए साल्मोनेला बैक्टीरिया के ओ एंटीजन और एच एंटीजन के सस्पेंशन का उपयोग करना शामिल है, जो एंटीबॉडी की उपस्थिति का संकेत देते हैं।
  * यह टेस्ट आमतौर पर संक्रमण के पहले सप्ताह के बाद किया जाता है जब एंटीबॉडी का पता लगाने के लिए रक्तप्रवाह में पर्याप्त स्तर में मौजूद होते हैं।
  * हालांकि विडल टेस्ट का व्यापक रूप से उपयोग किया जाता है, लेकिन इसे पूरी तरह से विशिष्ट या सटीक नहीं माना जाता है, और निदान के लिए कभी-कभी रक्त संस्कृति जैसे अन्य परीक्षणों के साथ पुष्टि की आवश्यकता हो सकती है।

  * टाइफाइड बुखार:
    * कारण: जीवाणु साल्मोनेला टाइफी, और कभी-कभी साल्मोनेला पैराटाइफी।
    * संचरण: दूषित भोजन या पानी के अंतर्ग्रहण के माध्यम से, अक्सर खराब स्वच्छता के कारण।
    * लक्षण: तेज बुखार, पेट दर्द, कमजोरी, सिरदर्द, भूख न लगना और कब्ज या दस्त। कुछ मामलों में एक विशिष्ट "गुलाब के धब्बे" जैसे चकत्ते दिखाई दे सकते हैं।
    * रोकथाम: बेहतर स्वच्छता, स्वच्छ पेयजल तक पहुंच और टाइफाइड के खिलाफ टीकाकरण।
    * उपचार: चिकित्सा पर्यवेक्षण के तहत सिप्रोफ्लोक्सासिन या एज़िथ्रोमाइसिन जैसे एंटीबायोटिक्स।
  * विकल्पों में उल्लिखित अन्य रोग:
    * मलेरिया: प्लास्मोडियम परजीवी के कारण होता है और संक्रमित एनोफिलीज मच्छरों के काटने से फैलता है। इसका निदान रक्त स्मीयर टेस्ट या रैपिड डायग्नोस्टिक टेस्ट का उपयोग करके किया जाता है।
    * एड्स: ह्यूमन इम्यूनोडेफिशिएंसी वायरस (एचआईवी) के कारण होता है। इसका निदान एचआईवी एंटीबॉडी का पता लगाने के लिए एलिसा या वेस्टर्न ब्लॉट जैसे परीक्षणों के माध्यम से किया जाता है।
  * टीबी के सामान्य लक्षणों में तीन सप्ताह से अधिक समय तक चलने वाली लगातार खांसी, सीने में दर्द, बुखार, रात में पसीना आना और बिना किसी स्पष्ट कारण के वजन कम होना शामिल हैं।
  * उचित निदान और एंटीबायोटिक दवाओं के एक कोर्स, जैसे कि आइसोनियाजिड और रिफैम्पिन के साथ क्षय रोग को रोका और ठीक किया जा सकता है।

  * संक्रामक रोग:
    * ये ऐसे रोग हैं जो जीवाणु, वायरस, कवक या परजीवी जैसे संक्रामक एजेंटों के कारण होते हैं।
    * वे प्रत्यक्ष संपर्क, हवाई संचरण या दूषित सतहों सहित विभिन्न तरीकों से एक व्यक्ति से दूसरे व्यक्ति में फैल सकते हैं।
    * उदाहरणों में मलेरिया, इन्फ्लुएंजा, एचआईवी/एड्स और हेपेटाइटिस शामिल हैं।
  * गैर-संक्रामक रोग (NCDs):
    * संक्रामक रोगों के विपरीत, NCDs संक्रामक नहीं होते हैं और एक व्यक्ति से दूसरे व्यक्ति में नहीं फैल सकते हैं।
    * उदाहरणों में मधुमेह, कैंसर, हृदय रोग और ऑस्टियोपोरोसिस शामिल हैं।
    * NCDs अक्सर आनुवंशिक, पर्यावरणीय या जीवनशैली कारकों के कारण होते हैं।
  * वैश्विक टीबी नियंत्रण प्रयास:
    * विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन (WHO) 2030 तक एक वैश्विक सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्य समस्या के रूप में क्षय रोग को समाप्त करने के लिए एंड टीबी रणनीति चलाता है।
    * भारत ने राष्ट्रीय क्षय रोग उन्मूलन कार्यक्रम (NTEP) लागू किया है, जिसका उद्देश्य प्रारंभिक पता लगाने, उपचार और जागरूकता अभियानों के माध्यम से 2025 तक टीबी को समाप्त करना है।
  * टीबी के लिए टीकाकरण:
    * बीसीजी वैक्सीन आमतौर पर बच्चों में क्षय रोग के गंभीर रूपों को रोकने के लिए प्रशासित किया जाता है।
    * जबकि टीका कुछ सुरक्षा प्रदान करता है, यह वयस्कों में टीबी संक्रमण को पूरी तरह से नहीं रोकता है।

Title: A Systematic and Validated Translation of the Perceived Empathy of Technology Scale to Chinese
Authors: Matthias Schmidmaier, Jingyao Zheng, Jie Song, Lik-Hang Lee, Sven Mayer
Date: Thu Oct 15 09:07:21 2026

The Perceived Empathy of Technology Scale (PETS) allows evaluation of empathic behavior in intelligent systems, a concept increasingly applied in human-AI interaction, particularly in emotional and mental health support applications. To support intercultural research and development, PETS is already available in multiple languages, as research suggests cultural and language-based differences in the expression and perception of empathy. Given the substantial Chinese-speaking population and the growing focus on cross-cultural HCI research, we present a validated translation of PETS into Putonghua (Mandarin) with Simplified Chinese. Based on established back-translation methodologies as used in previous PETS translations, our process included multiple independent translations, expert panel reviews, and empirical testing with a total of N=400 participants from an English and a Chinese sample. Through confirmatory factor analysis and invariance testing we show that the Chinese PETS retains the original two-factor structure with high reliability, with support for configural, metric, and scalar invariance. Beyond validation, empathic system behavior was rated equivalently across languages, while non-empathic behavior drew substantially higher ratings from Chinese participants, suggesting its absence is read less consistently across cultures than its presence. This validated Chinese version enables researchers and practitioners to assess empathy perceptions among Chinese-speaking users, supporting culturally appropriate empathic technology development.

Title: TRACER: A Multimodal Harness for Patient Care in Hospitals
Authors: Zane Durante, Paul Tang, Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran, Amit Kaushal, Shrinidhi Kowshika Lakshmikanth, Feolu Kolawole, Yu Jun Zheng, Yifan Geng, Shobhit Agarwal, Kevin Schulman, Juan Carlos Niebles, Ehsan Adeli, Arnold Milstein, Li Fei-Fei
Date: Thu Oct 15 05:00:47 2026

Continuous video and clinical records provide complementary information for understanding how patient behavior evolves over a hospital stay. A central challenge is how to represent behavior across the entire stay while preserving access to fine-grained visual and clinical evidence. We introduce TRACER, a training-free multimodal harness that constructs minute-level action records from video and combines them with clinical records into hourly reports. The harness equips an LLM agent with tools to query this hierarchy, inspect relevant video, and retrieve clinical records. To evaluate TRACER, we construct two benchmarks. The first contains 397 annotated one-minute clips spanning 15 atomic actions; the second poses 144 clinician-informed multiple-choice questions, grounded in 264 hours of video and clinical records from two ICU patients. TRACER achieves up to 84.8% accuracy for action detection and 61.0% QA accuracy versus 49.3% for the strongest baseline using the same backbone. Across 280 patients spanning approximately 60,000 camera-hours, TRACER identifies significantly less purposeful activity in patients with a positive delirium assessment during their stay than in those without (p < 0.0001). Our results show that combining continuous video with clinical records can support understanding of patient behavior over time and across patient cohorts without training on protected health data.

By Diana Bletter

Medical students at the Technion's American medical program get hands-on experience in a lab in August 2022. (Technion)

A record 1,649 students began medical studies in Israel this year, up about 14 percent from last year’s 1,448 enrolled students, the Health Ministry announces.

The surge follows data showing that some 1,370 Israeli physicians left the country for at least 12 months between 2023 and 2025, according to a recent Tel Aviv University study, raising widespread concern about a deepening brain drain in the national healthcare system.

In total, the number of medical students in Israel has jumped about 82% since 2021 following a joint initiative by the Health Ministry, the Council for Higher Education, the Planning and Budgeting Committee, and medical schools.

Cancer treatment
## Research

Clinical trials, also called research studies, test new treatments in people with cancer. The goal of this research is to find ways to treat cancer and help cancer patients. Clinical trials test many types of treatment such as new drugs, approaches to surgery or radiation therapy, new combinations of treatments, or new methods such as gene therapy. A clinical trial is one of the final stages of cancer research process. The search for new treatments begins in the laboratory, where scientists first develop and test new ideas. If an approach is promising, the next step may be testing a treatment in animals to see how it affects cancer in a living being, and whether it has harmful effects. Treatments that work well in the lab or in animals do not always work well in people. Studies are done with cancer patients to find out whether potential treatments are applicable to the population.

Patients who take part may be helped personally by the treatment they receive.

Bone cancer in cats and dogs
Condition in veterinary medicine

The most common bone tumor is called osteosarcoma, and typically affects middle-age to older dogs of large and giant breeds. Osteosarcoma is less common in cats. Osteosarcoma is an aggressive cancer that can develop in any bone of the body but the majority is seen in the limbs (e.g. long bones such as radius, humerus, femur, and tibia).

## Signs and symptoms

Dogs with limb osteosarcoma typically show lameness and swelling at the affected site. For other sites, dogs may show difficulty to open their mouth (if jaw bone cancer), nasal discharge (if nasal cavity bone cancer) or neurological signs (if spine bone cancer).

## Diagnosis

The initial evaluation involves radiographs (X-rays) of the affected site, but the only way to confirm the diagnosis is by sampling the tissue via biopsy or needle aspiration.

- Small Animal Clinical Oncology. W.B. Saunders Company.

## Treatment

Depending on the pet's unique condition, there are several treatment options, including surgery, chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Treating the pain adequately is also of crucial importance to improve the pet's quality of life, especially if amputation is not performed.

# Paccal Vet Feline Cancer Trial

Image: Black cat with green eyes sitting outdoors with blurred greenery in the background.

### A dose-finding study for cats with solid tumors

  * Fully funded study, no cost to pet owner

  * No placebo, all cats receive active treatment

  * Paccal Vet is based on a cancer drug widely used in human medicine

Participate

## Why is this study being done?

We are studying Paccal Vet as a possible new treatment option for cats with solid tumors.

Paccal Vet is a chemotherapy that has been specifically designed for pets, and it is based on a cancer drug that is widely used and approved in human cancer care.

Several clinical trials have been performed with Paccal Vet in dogs with promising results, but to date, no studies have evaluated Paccal Vet in cats.  

The purpose of this study is to test the tolerability of Paccal Vet in cats and to determine an acceptable dose. A secondary, exploratory goal is to see whether Paccal Vet may have anti-cancer activity in various tumors in cats.

## Why participate?

  * Give your cat access to a promising investigational drug based on a cancer drug that is widely used and approved in human cancer care

  * Benefit from regular medical check-ups and close monitoring during the study

  * Contributing to research that could benefit future feline cancer patients

【turn1063news34】 [wordlim: 100] Published: 6.0 years ago; Researchers are exploring the use of the cowpea mosaic virus (CPMV), a common plant virus, as an innovative cancer immunotherapy treatment. At Dartmouth College, veterinary oncologist Jack Hoopes has seen promising results when injecting virus-like particles derived from CPMV directly into tumors in dogs with oral cancer, leading to unexpectedly long remissions. The virus doesn't replicate in mammals but effectively stimulates the immune system to attack cancer cells. Collaborating with nanoengineer Nicole Steinmetz and immunologist Steve Fiering, the team discovered that CPMV triggers a strong immune response, reducing tumor growth and recurrence in mice and dogs.

Unlike traditional oncolytic viruses that directly kill cancer cells, CPMV works by mobilizing an immune response without replication, offering a safer and potentially more effective alternative. They've begun developing human trials and testing innovative delivery systems, including a virus-releasing implant for ovarian cancer. Despite challenges such as understanding why CPMV is so effective and navigating regulatory hurdles, early findings suggest plant virus-based cancer therapies could enhance existing treatments. Researchers have founded a company, Mosaic IE, to bring this therapy to human clinical trials, aiming to improve patient outcomes through combination therapies.

Marketed primarily for older or high-risk dogs, the test uses liquid biopsy technology—similar to methods used in humans—to detect multiple types of cancer from cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in blood samples. In a trial involving 1,100 dogs, the test detected 85% of aggressive cancers, though its overall accuracy was a more modest 55%. The test is safer and less invasive than surgical diagnostics and can potentially buy time for palliative care or early treatment.

However, experts caution against widespread use due to ethical concerns, cost implications, and risk of false positives (around 1.5%). Some are wary of overreliance on a test that isn’t fully transparent about its algorithms and may not significantly improve outcomes without accompanying treatments. A new longitudinal study of over 1,000 dogs is now underway to evaluate its potential for early detection over time. While support and commercial backing from Petco grows, many veterinarians, including bioethicists, stress the need for careful application. For pet owners like Marina Inserra, the test gave time and clarity to make informed decisions for her dog Cici, diagnosed early with terminal hemangiosarcoma.

Title: Assessing the Feasibility of Early Cancer Detection Using Routine Laboratory Data: An Evaluation of Machine Learning Approaches on an Imbalanced Dataset
Authors: Shumin Li
Date: Thu Oct 23 04:52:42 2025

The development of accessible screening tools for early cancer detection in dogs represents a significant challenge in veterinary medicine. Routine laboratory data offer a promising, low-cost source for such tools, but their utility is hampered by the non-specificity of individual biomarkers and the severe class imbalance inherent in screening populations. This study assesses the feasibility of cancer risk classification using the Golden Retriever Lifetime Study (GRLS) cohort under real-world constraints, including the grouping of diverse cancer types and the inclusion of post-diagnosis samples. A comprehensive benchmark evaluation was conducted, systematically comparing 126 analytical pipelines that comprised various machine learning models, feature selection methods, and data balancing techniques. Data were partitioned at the patient level to prevent leakage.

# 〖法說會備忘錄〗共信-KY 20250730

發布日：2025/08/05

字級

本報告內容使用 AI 技術，根據 台灣證券交易所及櫃買中心法說會之官方影音檔 進行摘要整理。本文件的目標是協助讀者快速理解各公司法說會之重點，包括營運狀況、財務表現及未來展望。

  * 核心業務：共信-KY 是一家專注於研發抗癌藥物的公司，其核心技術為微創靶向腫瘤消融（MITA）。主要產品為化學小分子藥物 PTS 注射液，可直接注射於腫瘤內部，透過干擾癌細胞的脂筏（Lipid Raft）穩定性及調控腫瘤微環境，選擇性地誘導癌細胞凋亡與壞死，而對正常細胞損傷較小。公司營運總部位於台灣，並設有美國子公司及天津子公司（中國藥證持有人）。
  * 主要產品線：
    * 人體用藥：
      * 普羅仙安 (PTS302)：用於治療中央型氣道阻塞肺癌，已於 2023 年 8 月在中國上市。
      * 惡性胸腔積液 (PTS500)：已完成恩慈療法並於美國臨床腫瘤學會（ASCO）發表成果，顯示 75% 的控制率與 93 天的無惡化存活期 (PFS)，即將在台灣申請二期、美國申請二/三期臨床試驗，並已吸引國際藥廠洽談。
      * 頭頸癌：恩慈療法展現良好效果，能保留器官功能，已與台北馬偕醫院合作展開 IIT 實驗。
      * 罕見「軟組織肉瘤」 (PTS02)：已獲美國 FDA 孤兒藥資格，預計 2025Q3 向 FDA 提交樞紐試驗申請。
## 5. 營運策略與未來發展

  * 長期規劃：
    * 成為微創消融領域領導者：目標是將微創靶向腫瘤消融技術（MITA）推廣為全球癌症治療的標準指南（Guidance）之一。
    * 擴大適應症開發：公司擁有 22 項適應症專利，目前僅開發了四至五項，未來將持續投入資源開發剩餘的專利，拓展產品應用。
    * 建立美國營運基地：透過成立美國子公司並完成募資，加速罕見軟組織肉瘤與惡性胸腔積液在美國的臨床開發與上市進程。
  * 競爭優勢：
    * 獨特作用機制：PTS 具備選擇性識別並殺傷癌細胞的能力，對正常組織傷害小。
    * 保留器官功能：與傳統手術相比，可避免大面積切除，保留病人生活品質，在頭頸癌等領域尤具優勢。
## 6. 展望與指引

  * 短期營運催化劑：
    * 2025Q3：犬科黑色素瘤用藥 GWA103 有望取得台灣藥證，並開始出貨。
    * 2025Q3：向美國 FDA 遞交軟組織肉瘤（孤兒藥）的樞紐試驗申請。
    * 2025 下半年：皮膚凝膠 GW046 在台上市；啟動台灣惡性胸腔積液二期臨床試驗。
    * 中國市場：醫保及商保申請若取得進展，將顯著帶動普羅仙安的銷售。
  * 中長期成長動能：
    * 美國市場：惡性胸腔積液用藥 PTS500 的二/三期臨床試驗將於 2026 年在美國申請，此為一項潛在的重磅產品。
    * 國際授權：惡性胸腔積液產品已開始與國際藥廠洽談授權，是未來重要的潛在收入來源。
    * 動物用藥全球佈局：以台灣藥證為基礎，拓展至澳洲、日本、美國等主要寵物市場。

# 共信-KY動物抗癌新藥申請台灣藥證 明年H2有望取得藥證

鉅亨網記者劉玟妤 台北2024-07-31 10:28

Image: AI gen LogoAI新聞摘要

  * 共信 - KY(6617-TW) 宣布旗下動物靶向腫瘤消融新藥「思沛康注射液」正式送出申請台灣藥證，正式進軍寵物市場。共信 - KY 表示，從申請到取得許可大約需 6 至 10 個月，因此有望在 2025 年上半年取得藥證。 

共信 - KY(6617-TW) 宣布旗下動物靶向腫瘤消融新藥「思沛康注射液」正式送出申請台灣藥證，正式進軍寵物市場。共信 - KY 表示，從申請到取得許可大約需 6 至 10 個月，因此有望在 2025 年上半年取得藥證。 

根據台灣經濟研究院統計，截至 2022 年台灣的貓狗新飼養登記數量達 18 萬隻，遠超過每年 10 萬的新生兒。此外，根據 Global Market Insights 的數據，2022 年全球寵物產業市值約 2610 億美元，預計到 2027 年將成長至 3500 億美元，年複合成長率 (CAGR) 高達 6.1%。共信 - KY 認為，毛孩經濟有望成為台灣下個兆元產業。 

共信 - KY 鎖定伴侶動物疾病市場，針對犬類黑色素腫瘤部位注射治療，獲得初步臨床試驗成效，並於正式提交農業部，申請寵物抗癌用藥。 

共信 - KY 指出，截至目前為止，在全球伴侶動物抗癌用藥市場上，仍有相當大的市場需求，主要原因為目前對於伴侶動物罹患癌症的治療方式，仍是以手術搭配化療為主。不過這樣的標準治療對於動物傷害大，且無法滿足因為少子化、老年化社會將犬貓視為家庭伴侶的關愛需求，共信 - KY 的 PTS 藥物具有靶向腫瘤消融特性，可望滿足此市場趨勢。 

法人也看好，未來寵物癌症的市場潛力，未來在靶向腫瘤消融新藥「思沛康注射液」成功上市銷售後，可望為共信 - KY 再添營收成長動能。
